Accordingly, our respective Governments, through representatives assembled in the city of San Francisco, who have exhibited their full powers found to be in good and due form, have agreed to the present Charter of the United Nations and do hereby establish an international organization to be known as the United Nations.

related.title: US resumes daylight strikes on Iran as tensions escalate over Strait of Hormuz
related.summary: US military has resumed its air strikes against Iran in broad daylight on Wednesday, as Washington said it was intensifying its campaign aimed at limiting Tehran’s ability to threaten commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. CENTCOM said the strikes were intended to further reduce Iran’s ability to attack commercial vessels passing through the strategic waterway.
bullets: US military has resumed its air strikes against Iran in broad daylight on Wednesday, as Washington said it was intensifying its campaign aimed at limiting Tehran’s ability to threaten commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
CENTCOM said the strikes were intended to further reduce Iran’s ability to attack commercial vessels passing through the strategic waterway.

However, the continuation of the attacks and the start of a new wave of strikes in the middle of the day indicate Washington's intent to pursue a prolonged military campaign around the clock, limiting the other side’s ability to recover and respond while rapidly degrading Iran’s strategic infrastructure.
An Iranian Health Ministry official said overnight US airstrikes injured more than 260 people, including three women and six people under the age of 18.
Previously, Iran’s Health Ministry had said that 17 people had been killed and more than 115 injured during US strikes targeting six Iranian cities.

related.summary: Normalising the killing Since the “ceasefire” agreement took effect, Israel has conditioned the international community to accept daily breaches and killings in Gaza as the new normal, effectively acting as if the pact does not restrict its military freedom, analysts said. Furthermore, the humanitarian situation continues to deteriorate under the ceasefire, with Israel allowing only 35 percent of the expected aid trucks and 36 percent of permitted travellers to cross the borders.

Despite a months-long “ceasefire”, Israel continues to launch deadly raids across the Palestinian territory, citing the presence of Hamas fighters and “imminent threats”.

These killings, they warn, could systematically derail the United States-backed plan for a post-war Gaza, paralyse the so-called Board of Peace set up under the Trump administration plan, and effectively allow Israel to maintain indefinite control over a territory that is otherwise uninhabitable.
The United Nations Human Rights Office (OHCHR) reported that Israeli attacks are systematically targeting police officers, whose role is essential for civic order and any future reconstruction.

related.title: Spillover Effects: How the Middle East crisis threatens food security - Focus on Myanmar (Date Released: 9 July 2026 / Reporting period: Week of 29 June)
related.summary: While recent pauses in military exchanges and indirect negotiations have reduced immediate violence, disruptions to the Strait of Hormuz—through which around one-fifth of global oil supply flows—have already triggered sharp increases in energy prices, supply chain instability, and rising inflation worldwide. Overview The Iran–United States crisis in 2026 has evolved from a high-intensity conflict into a fragile and uncertain de-escalation phase, but its global repercussions remain significant and ongoing.
bullets: While recent pauses in military exchanges and indirect negotiations have reduced immediate violence, disruptions to the Strait of Hormuz—through which around one-fifth of global oil supply flows—have already triggered sharp increases in energy prices, supply chain instability, and rising inflation worldwide.

Overview The Iran–United States crisis in 2026 has evolved from a high-intensity conflict into a fragile and uncertain de-escalation phase, but its global repercussions remain significant and ongoing.

These shocks are particularly severe for energy-importing and developing economies, contributing to slower global growth, higher food and commodity prices, and increased economic vulnerability across Asia.

Myanmar faces especially deep impacts due to its heavy dependence on imported fuel (around 9095% of supply), limited reserves, and fragile economic conditions; the crisis has led to rising fuel prices, shortages, currency depreciation, and increased costs of transportation, food, and agricultural production.

As a result, the conflict is not only a geopolitical issue but also a major economic shock, disproportionately affecting vulnerable countries like Myanmar, where it intensifies inflation, threatens livelihoods, and exacerbates existing economic instability.
